sweep.label: Granite-4.0-H-Tiny: the D29 frontier - stage granularity x chip capacity x bank depth
sweep.enumeration: DIRECTIONAL STEP-UP LADDER (P7.4): from the declared initializer, one axis one rung at a time, outward in both directions; every point visited is evaluated in full and recorded, and the walk is deterministic. Never a blind cross product.

entries.label: pipeline beat (one token exits per beat)
entries.basis: the MEDIAN of the SETTLED TAIL of the measured intervals between consecutive token exits: 2 of the 4 measured interval(s). One interval is held out as the traversal that entered at beat 0 and travelled through a filling pipeline (nothing queued behind it, so its exit lands early), and a further 1 interval(s) are dropped as RAMP because they do not agree with the tail's own median to 1e-03. Both sets are printed above rather than smoothed in, and the tail rule is what makes the reported beat independent of how many beats the window lowered (P7.9). An exit is the finish of the last op of a completed traversal on the one timeline, so the beat is a difference of two timeline readings and never a max-stage-time formula (A1, P4 3).

entries.label: steady throughput = 1 / beat (HEADLINE)
entries.basis: D29's identity, on the measured beat: the pipeline is always full, so exactly ONE token leaves the last stage per beat and the system rate is 1/beat. The beat is the median of the SETTLED TAIL (2 interval(s)) of the 4 measured inter-exit intervals; the fill transient and any still-ramping intervals are held out and printed beside it, and this headline is only a settled measurement when pipeline.beat_converged is true — the run says so by name when it is not. Nothing here is a period times a count.

entries.label: per-stream token rate
entries.basis: 1 / (D x beat) with D = 10 resident streams (D29). A stream gets the machine once every D beats, which is the price of keeping the pipeline full.

entries.label: resident streams D (= pipeline stages)
entries.basis: the stage count, DERIVED from the chip partition (default: one stage per analog chip). D29 makes D a consequence of the stage plan, never a configured batch — the serving surface refuses a batch by name.

entries.label: per-token latency (one stream's traversal of the pipeline)
entries.basis: finish of traversal 4's last op minus the issue of its first, both read off the one timeline: the wall time one stream needs to walk every stage and emit one token. D29's identity says this is D x beat; the identity residual is reported in the pipeline block rather than replacing the measurement.

extrapolation.basis: DECODE_LEN x D x BEAT. A request occupies one stream and gets a token every D beats, so its decode phase is decode_len x D x beat. This is an EXTRAPOLATION — a period times a count — so it lives here, labeled, and never enters metrics[] (P4 3, ADJ-6). Prefill is not in it: D25/D29 make the mapped run decode-only and the streams arrive already prefilled.

disclosures.value: probe beat 3.73681e-05 s, CONVERGED (3 settled interval(s), 0 dropped as ramp, whole steady sample spread 0.0225%)
disclosures.reason: The width above is derived from the PROBE pass's beat, and that beat is a measurement like any other. Streams that enter too late to finish inside the window are lowered as far as the window reaches and their partial work is on the timeline, contending, exactly as it would in the machine.

disclosures.reason: The exits were still SETTLING inside the lowered window: the fill allowance of D - 1 beats is exact only when every stage has the same service time, and this run's stage plan is uneven, so a stream can wait on a slower stage and the exits take longer than D - 1 beats to become periodic. The dropped intervals are printed in the pipeline block as ramp_beat_intervals_s and the whole steady sample spreads 20.2% about the beat. Reading the beat off the tail instead of the median of the whole sample is what makes the headline independent of the window size; the alternative measured 12% higher on Granite-4.0-H-Tiny at decode_window 2. Nothing is padded and no interval is smoothed — the ramp is named, not averaged.
